findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: Input with unexpected length or padding
findings.assumptions: The input length (src_len) is not checked against the actual length of the base64 encoded string. The base64 decoding process may write beyond the allocated buffer if the input is malformed.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: Malformed base64 input that could lead to unexpected behavior or execution of arbitrary code
findings.assumptions: The base64_digits array is used to map characters to their respective values. If the input contains unexpected characters, it may lead to undefined behavior, including execution of arbitrary code.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: Input with unexpected length or padding
findings.assumptions: The input length (src_len) is not checked against the actual length of the base64 encoded string. The base64 decoding process may write beyond the allocated buffer if the input is malformed.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.trigger: Large src_len value that causes overflow in memory allocation
findings.assumptions: The memory allocation size is calculated as src_len / 4 * 3 + 1. If src_len is very large, this calculation may overflow, leading to insufficient memory allocation.
